analyst_view.overall: Early view: Como are the story of the competition, 4th with 9 points after a record 9-1 win at Lens in which Tasos Douvikas scored a hat-trick, although they lost 2-0 at Inter in Serie A on 8 November. AEK Athens (29th, 3 points) pushed Real Madrid hard before losing 3-2, but their scorer that night, Aboubakary Koita, was sent off in stoppage time and is banned for this game (the ban has not yet been served).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean a little higher. Como scored nine at Lens with seven different scorers, and AEK conceded three to Real Madrid at home, so I expect Como to create plenty. AEK also lose Koita, who scored against Madrid, which makes their own goal harder to find but does little to slow Como.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Como will dominate the ball, which pushes their share up, but they score so much from open play (only one of the nine at Lens was a header from Marc-Oliver Kempf) that corner pressure builds less than usual. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and I lean slightly lower. Como's 9-1 at Lens produced only two bookings, both for Lens, as one-sided games tend to. AEK may foul more chasing the ball, but this looks more like a game of three or four cards than five.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and I lean higher. Cesc Fabregas's Como have attacked relentlessly in Europe, and AEK without Koita lose an outlet to relieve pressure. Most of the total should come from the home side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target and I lean higher. Como's attack (Douvikas, Nico Paz, Martin Baturina) is in form and AEK's defence leaked three to Madrid. I expect Como alone to account for most of ten or more efforts on goal.
